section.title: Data Format Standards

question.text: Data Format Standards

json.answer:
In order to allow for interoperability, reproducibility, and reuse, all data will be stored and saved in
standard and open formats. Experimental characterization data will be stored and saved as, e.g.,
ASCII, CSV, Word, Matlab and Python files. Microscope images will be stored as portable graphic
files (.tif, .jpg or .png format). Crystallographic data will be reported in standard crystallographic

section.title: information framework (*.cif) format to facilitate visualization and further analysis through widely

question.text: information framework (*.cif) format to facilitate visualization and further analysis through widely

json.answer:
available software tools (VESTA, cif2file, etc.). Crystallographic data for previously-unreported
compounds/structures will be uploaded to the ICSD database. First principles simulation input and
output files (generated with the VASP and CRYSTAL codes) will be stored as rich text format (*.rtf)
files for readability across many programs and platforms. The CRYSTAL code manual will be

section.title: Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and production of derivatives

question.text: Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and production of derivatives

json.answer:
All data will be stored in Dryad and will be available under a public domain, creative commons
license (CC0). Note that while a personal ORCID is needed to deposit data in Dryad, no ORCID is
required to search, find and download datasets.
The existing open source software infrastructure within CASM that serves as a foundation to this
project, is already licensed by the Regents of the University of California under the ``LGPL'' open

section.title: source license, and distributed via the prisms-center conda channel, permitting non-exclusive use of

question.text: source license, and distributed via the prisms-center conda channel, permitting non-exclusive use of

json.answer:
the software. Additions to CASM will be released as LGPL to follow the current licensing of
CASM.

section.title: Archiving of Data, Samples, and Other Relevant Research Products

question.text: Archiving of Data, Samples, and Other Relevant Research Products

json.answer:
Laboratory notebooks and samples will be retained for a minimum of 5 years following the
conclusion of the program and will remain the property of UC Santa Barbara and kept on campus
after students graduate. All digital data produced over the course of the project and stored on Box
will be moved to Dryad after completion of the project for indefinite storage (>5 years).
